newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent weaker as June loading cuts disappoint.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent weaker as June loading cuts disappoint.

text.p: The North Sea Brent cash market eased lower on Thursday with the June Brent loading programme heavier than some traders had expected.
Signs that a recent narrowing of refining margins was pushing refiners towards cutting runs also pressured the Brent market, traders said.
The June/July Brent intermonth spreads slipped a few cents to trade twice at +5 cents, while July/August was heard traded weaker at +2 cents.
IPE June Brent, which expires on Thursday, was trading 10 cents down at $19.41 a barrel at 1200 GMT.
A CFD for next week traded at July Brent - 23 cents, some five cents down from Wednesday's levels. A CFD for the month of June traded at July Brent -21 cents.
The June Brent loading programme scheduled the equivalent of 38.4 cargoes, including top ups, down from the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes in May.
Some traders were expecting an even lighter loading programme because of maintenance at many of the Brent-Ninian systems fields and a shorter month.
"The market's softer because the Brent programme isn't too much changed from last month," a trader said.
Brent system operator Shell Expro said on Thursday that it had cancelled maintenance at the 55,000 barrel per day Tern field, originally scheduled for June 22-28.
The last of the May Brent dates passed through the chains on Wednesday.
The Norwegian Ekofisk programme, also released on Thursday, scheduled 36 cargoes for June, two up from May.
News that Texaco plans to cut crude throughput at its Rotterdam refinery by 20 percent in the second half of May was also depressing the market, traders said.

Reuters data shows simple hydroskimming margins for a typical Rotterdam refinery turned negative earlier this week and complex cracking margins were faring little better, falling from over $2 a barrel at the start of the month to around $1.30 a barrel on Thursday.
